method: Author-scanned Portuguese poetic syllables, counted through the last stressed syllable. Underscores mark synalepha; finalUncountedSyllables removes posttonic syllables after the last stress. No Spanish final-word adjustment or Russian vowel counter is used.
status: Immediately edited provisional literary draft; independent review pending
semanticDecisions: The rear/leg-fluid/ground-watering poem retains all three images. Bumbum is a colloquial rear euphemism; the two quoted movie lines and the emphatic final-line callback use identical wording.

The Violet poem retains tender licking, cleaning the speaker's mess, and his renewed erection. Portuguese subject omission is resolved by the preceding explicit dedication to Violet and the first-person estou in the last line.
The drink-and-friends poem preserves the singular-to-plural correction in equal five-syllable lines. Drinques uses its ordinary Portuguese two-syllable form.

The bridge poem retains shaping the ground, crossing above violent waters, and uniting our friends. Unir nossos amigos makes the source possession explicit in five poetic syllables, with sos_a synalepha and the final posttonic gos uncounted. Branch themes and all 27 possible line combinations remain unchanged.
Penny remains a falcon. Falcão, que beleza avoids attributing masculine personal gender to her while preserving admiration; the next lines retain flight above clouds and an unvisited destination.

The busy little insect remains an insetinho; a mil expresses busyness. Its priorities and present work are questioned. Lida denotes work; agora preserves the temporal contrast behind the relaxed-life feedback.
The river poem retains ceaseless movement, an endless journey and the flowing river. It supports the full water/time explanation without adding an answer to its speculative reincarnation question.
All mixed choices retain the source's possible thematic mismatch. No branch identities, controls, conditions, timing or resource keys are adapted.
